column1: # Each test's seconds and processor seconds in Self Coverage on Linux: the
# most it took in either of two full runs (45811808363 and 45833849393,
# 2026-11-26), each run's from the test-seconds.tsv its slices keep, a name
# in two binaries summed. The slices are dealt by the larger of the two. CI's
# plan reads the most of main's last three runs (the `test-seconds` artifact
# Self Coverage keeps), which outrank these: this file stands in only where
# no run kept them. Refresh from the runs' slices:
#   cat run-*/test-seconds.tsv | awk -F'\t' '{ w[$1] += $2; c[$1] += $3 } END { for (n in w) printf "%s\t%.1f\t%.1f\n", n, w[n], c[n] }' | LC_ALL=C sort
